text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In the prelude to Prime Minister John Howard's first prime ministerial visit to China, scheduled for the end of March, China is thawing the chill in its relations with Australia and is offering trade concessions and ending an unannounced ban on high-level visits. Page 1.

Under a plan developed by the Federal Government's Rsearch and Development Board to pump investment into emerging high-growth companies, the Coalition looks set to spend more than A$130 million to boost Australia's dormant venture capital industry. Under the scheme, the Goernment would contribute A$2 for every A$1 invested by the private sector in qualifying venture capital funds. Page 1.

Former Prime Minister Paul Keating told a Merrill Lynch investment conference in Hong Kong this week that the temptation in Asian societies to turn inwards was a "dangerous self-delusion", saying that continued growth depended on "The Three Opens" - open conomies, open societies and an open region. Page 2.

Defying a warning from Prime Minister John Howard that any use of foreign mercenaries against Bougainville rebels would be "absolutely and completely unacceptable", Papua New Guinean Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan last night confirmed and defended his Government's decision to use the mercenaries, saying they would be used only to train PNG special forces. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard intensified pressure on the Papua New Guinea Government yesterday to dump a plan to use foreign mercenaries, from Sandline International, in the conflict on Bougainville, saying the plan was "absolutely and completely unacceptable". Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan claims the mercenaries were engaged solely to train the country's soldiers. Page 1.

Donald McDonald, the chairman of the ABC board, yesterday backed the national broadcaster's managing director Brian Johns over the controversial screening of an ACTU-sponsored lecture by former Labor prime minister Gough Whitlam - only for the ABC to be attacked by Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer, who said the board would receive a "rude shock" if it were aware of rural and regional views of the broadcaster. Page 1.

Taxation Commissioner Michael Carmody announced yesterday that the Australian Taxation Office is preparing reforms to the tax collection system, including the use of "tax spies", to avoid a repeat of last month's Budget black hole. Carmody said fundamental change was required because the tax office could no longer protect Australia's tax base through the traditional self-assessment tax system. Page 1.

Following the creation at Edinburgh's Roslin Institute of a sheep that is an identical twin of its mother, Ron Trent, the chairman of the Gene Therapy Committee of the National Health and Medical Research Council, says there are no obvious reasons for the technology to be used to clone a human. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Papua New Guinea's decision to use foreign mercenaries on the sessionist island of Bougainville follows Australia's refusal to provide Papua New Guinea with satellite technology which could reportedly could have been used to pinpoint the source of Bougainille Revolutionary Army radio broadcasts. Page 1.

Nicole Smith told the Supreme Court yesterday during her negligence suit against Dr Sushil Anand, Dr Eric Farmer, Dr Ameen Bham and two pathology laboratories the misdiagnosis of a melanoma had greatly shortened her life expectancy. Smith is 30 years old, has a three-and-a-half year-old daughter, and has just months to live. Page 1.

The New South Wales Royal Commission was told yesterday of an investigation into allegations of child abuse that was botched from beginning to end. The ineptitude of both the Police and Department of Community Services officers was to blame for a case involving two girls, aged four and five, who separately told their mothers they were being sexually abused by the de-facto partner of their after-school carer, never reaching court. Page 1.

Under a plan which has been condemned by the Opposition and minor parties as one which could create a giant "slush fund", funds from the Federal Government's A$1 billion Natural Heritage Fund will be spent at the direction of two Cabinet ministers - the Evironment Minister and Primary Industries and Energy Minister - without independent environmental advice. Page 1.
THE AGE

The Immigration Department confirmed yesterday the Federal Government banned two Russians - believed to be employees of an aircraft manufacturer - from entering Australia for the Avalon air show last week because they posed a risk to national security. It is believed that visas were withheld on the advice of the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation. Page 1.

Only hours after Prime Minister John Howard intensified criticism of Papua New Guinean plans to hire African-based mercenaries to assassinate rebel leaders on Bougainville, Papua New Guinea's Prime Minister, Sir Julius Chan, issued a statement last night aying he expected Australian leaders to be more sensitive. Page 1.

Professor Kwong Lee Dow, the new chairman of the Board of Studies, which sets curriculum and standards for Victorian schools, has rejected rumours that the State Government wants to make the Victorian Certificate of Education a one-year course, saying the Year 11 component of the course could be enhanced. Page 1.

Health authorities have issued a hepatitis A warning following the death of a 77-year-old man who is believed to have eaten oysters from the Wallis Lake on the mid-north coast of New South Wales, and reports of 36 new cases of the virus in Victoria since riday - bringing the number of cases in the State this year to 117. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
